sources.reason: Annotated original monitor for keyboard, display, memory and cassette I/O. Upstream assembly/ROM comparison workflow exists; no independent byte match.

Annotated 1987 rescue-helicopter game with monitor calls and gameplay data. Repository includes higher-level experiments; native 8080 listing remains distinct. Upstream byte-exact claim not independently tested.
Annotated Ladder game with named monitor calls, PRNG state, tile codes and level data. Retains original author credit and distinguishes annotations from original game content.
Fabrizio Di Vittorio Bondwell SPEECH.COM disassembly retargeted to M80/L80 and Cromemco D+7A output. IMSAI host naming does not prove an 8080-only build; inspected source is Z80-derived.
REV02-focused code/resource analysis with main-68000 and named Z80 sound driver. Requires supplied ROM; differences from REV00 not fully established.
DISA listing, index and original extension file with named BASIC command table and mostly numeric code labels. Limited semantic annotation; not a claim of fully understood source.

REV02 disassembly with hardware includes, graphics/audio and emulator build workflows. One generated include says Processor 68020; this is a disassembler setting, not evidence the Mega Drive game requires 68020.

Merged UW1/UW2 reconstruction with semantic routines and native/web ports. README says prior UW1Decomp/UW2Decomp repositories moved here. Matching and parity claims retained as upstream reports, not independently measured.

Watcom matching project with substantive C replacements and many INCLUDE_ASM fallbacks. Byte-identical whole-image relinking does not mean the game is fully decompiled; upstream reports only a subset of functions replaced.

Semantic source and function-level matching reports. Upstream 100% matched count includes 53 assembly stand-ins and 79 functions from Watcom libraries; matching is not 100% recovered C. No independent toolchain run.
Substantial SDL2/decompiler-derived experiment, explicitly nonfunctional and buggy. Rendering and loop changes are documented; do not label this a working faithful port.
Source-derived actor physics, levels and original EGA/PC-speaker handling. Requires original resource files but not DOS executable at runtime; parity is upstream, not independently verified.
Assembler written for IDA output from Robotron research, with 6800/6809 instruction tables and expression evaluator. Robotron disassembly itself is not included; do not classify tool as game source.

Partial annotated listing and exploratory game modifications. Author explicitly acknowledges uncertain 6809/hardware understanding; numeric labels and hypotheses are not established full semantic recovery.
Short commented position-independent routine recovered from embedded BASIC machine-code DATA, explaining ROM/RAM mapping and interrupt handling. Narrow utility, not complete system ROM.

Annotated main/sound/vector/banked sources and original-ROM patching tools, independent of the bundled emulator. Hardware Slapstic-removal proposal is explicitly untested. Claude credited; no independent full byte comparison.
Original source with named IRQ, input, sprite and game state; historical build environment not independently reproduced.
Original bitmap-adventure source with scrolling macros, historically cross-assembled on BBC ADE. Toolchain history is not the game's target platform.
Author's backup corpus with PDS source, sprite multiplexing and separate tape/disk loaders. README explicitly says modern rebuilding is not fully worked out.
Author-preserved game, display and table source with sprite-duplication technique and BBC cross-development history. No independent rebuild.
Original PDS-formatted source with binary headers and preserved game code. Base64 inspection recovered readable enemy-control instructions without treating headers as corruption; build not attempted.

David Maynard's source recovered from original disks and released with permission. Atari and C64 text sources are preserved alongside disk images; Atari source disks require ValForth and are not bootable games.

Commented/reorganized GEOS 2.0 KERNAL and drivers. Upstream deliberately optimizes/revises code; sampled burst driver notes remaining bugs. Not blanket original-byte or universal hardware compatibility.
Historical MINIX tree with Atari-specific kernel, WD1772 floppy/DMA and device drivers. Distinct 1.5 lineage retained separately from later 2.0.2 adaptation.
Later MINIX adaptation includes Atari conditional kernel drivers and enhanced floppy handling. Multi-platform source tree does not mean every target was built or tested.

Transcribed 1979 paper source with annotated/listing/assembler-source forms and generation rules. Distinct historical transcription, not the separately tracked modifications or higher-level recreation.
Ezra Dreisbach source released with permission under GPL, including sector/AI/rendering code. Game data absent; engine source does not establish a self-contained playable game.
Restoration of released original source with entity routines and modern RMAC/RLN build flow. Original ROM needed for assets; README says binary matching is not current goal and entity issues remain.
USA/Japan matching project with substantive combat calculations and filesystem routines. Recompilable completeness is a goal; version tables and progress badges do not establish full-game completion.
Early matching project with actor/base sources. README explicitly says it cannot compile to a full ROM yet; do not imply a playable reconstruction.
Driver-format research and MIDI extraction tool with sequence/channel documentation. Several commands unknown and converter tempo is approximate; not a complete driver reconstruction.
C driver implementation with PS1 libspu transfer callbacks, instrument and sequencer structures. Early source research; no independently verified matching or runtime completeness.
Native 6502 portal-rendering code, map/display buffers and support tooling. Sparse README supplemented with source inspection; not a completed game or a desktop Doom engine.

Substantive board-family analysis and MAME driver repairs, but its primary delivered restoration is emulation. Retain in audit backlog rather than promoting as a native source port; separately review the reusable disassembly output.
Inspected add_vertex command has empty apply and undo bodies. Engine boom is promoted, but the editor needs more implementation evidence before classification as a usable tool.

notes: Parent-only pass across 28 broad platform/type search lanes. URL and title/lineage screening against latest catalogue; prior reviewed exclusions and aliases were not resubmitted. Inspected pinned README/tree and representative source. Extensionless, PDS, .tas and Forth sources were handled explicitly. One PDS file required base64 inspection because its historical binary header is not UTF-8; no source executed. Large-source empty response was replaced by bounded hardware-include inspection. Matching relink, assembly stand-ins and decompiled functions are distinguished. Copyright/toolchain/asset caveats retained. TCH emulation-focused restoration held for audit rather than presented as native port.
